derivations.claim: Setup and coherence: let $A=k[x]$, $X=\operatorname{Spec}A$, $M=A/(x)$ and $\mathcal F=\widetilde M$. By [F1] the ring $A$ is a principal ideal domain, hence Noetherian, so $X$ is locally Noetherian; the class of $1$ generates $M$, so $M$ is finitely generated and $\mathcal F$ is quasi-coherent of finite type by [F2], hence coherent on $X$ by the coherence theorem of [F2]. [F1, F2]

Stalks: for a prime $\mathfrak p\in X$ the isomorphisms $\mathcal F_{\mathfrak p}\cong M_{\mathfrak p}\cong A_{\mathfrak p}/xA_{\mathfrak p}$ hold by [F2] and [F3]. If $\mathfrak p\neq(x)$ then $x\notin\mathfrak p$ by [F1], so $x$ is a unit of $A_{\mathfrak p}$ by [F3] and therefore $xA_{\mathfrak p}=A_{\mathfrak p}$ and $\mathcal F_{\mathfrak p}=0$; in particular $\mathcal F_\eta=0$ for the generic point $\eta=(0)$, which is distinct from $(x)$ by [F1]. [F1, F2, F3]

The generic point lies in every nonempty open subset: by [F7] the closure of $\{(0)\}$ is $V((0))=X$, since every prime of the domain $A$ contains $(0)$. If $U\subseteq X$ were a nonempty open set with $(0)\notin U$, then $X\setminus U$ would be a closed set containing $(0)$, hence would contain $\overline{\{(0)\}}=X$, contradicting $U\neq\varnothing$; therefore $(0)\in U$ for every nonempty open $U\subseteq X$. [F7]

Fibres of free module sheaves on distinguished opens: for every $f\in A$, putting $V=D(f)$, the localisation $A\to A_f$ identifies $V$ with $\operatorname{Spec}A_f$ as locally ringed spaces by [F6], so the free sheaf $\mathcal O_V^r$ is the free module sheaf of rank $r$ on $\operatorname{Spec}A_f$; applying [F5] with $B=A_f$ gives $(\mathcal O_V^r)(y)\cong\kappa(y)^r$ at every $y\in V$, a vector space of dimension $r$ over the residue field $\kappa(y)$. [F5, F6]

Fibre at the closed point: at $\mathfrak p=(x)$ steps 1.2 and [F3] give $\mathcal F_{(x)}\cong A_{(x)}/xA_{(x)}=\kappa((x))\cong k$, the residue field of the local ring $A_{(x)}$, whose maximal ideal is $xA_{(x)}$ by [F1]; this maximal ideal annihilates $\mathcal F_{(x)}$, so the fibre is $\mathcal F((x))\cong\mathcal F_{(x)}/\mathfrak m_{(x)}\mathcal F_{(x)}\cong k$ by [F4], a one-dimensional $\kappa((x))$-vector space. [F1, F3, F4, step 1.2]
Fibre at the generic point: since $\eta=(0)\neq(x)$, step 1.2 gives $\mathcal F_\eta=0$, hence the fibre $\mathcal F(\eta)=0$ by [F4]. [F4, step 1.2]

A free chart at the closed point: assume now that $\mathcal F$ is finite locally free in the sense of [F8]. Then at the point $(x)$ there are an open neighbourhood $U\ni(x)$ and an integer $r\ge0$ with $\mathcal F|_U\cong\mathcal O_U^r$; by [F6] choose $f\in A$ with $(x)\in D(f)\subseteq U$ and put $V=D(f)$, so that restricting the isomorphism gives $\mathcal F|_V\cong\mathcal O_V^r$. Since $V$ is a nonempty open subset of $X$, step 1.3 gives $\eta=(0)\in V$. [F6, F8, step 1.3]

First rank constraint: the fibre of a restriction is the fibre by [F4], so steps 2.2 and 1.4 give $\kappa(\eta)^r\cong(\mathcal O_V^r)(\eta)=(\mathcal F|_V)(\eta)=\mathcal F(\eta)=0$; since $\kappa(\eta)$ is a field, $\kappa(\eta)^r=0$ forces $r=0$. [F4, step 2.2, step 1.4]

Second rank constraint: likewise steps 2.1 and 1.4 give $\mathcal F((x))=(\mathcal F|_V)((x))=(\mathcal O_V^r)((x))\cong\kappa((x))^r$, of $\kappa((x))$-dimension $r$; but by step 2.1 the fibre $\mathcal F((x))$ is one-dimensional over $\kappa((x))$, so $r=1$. [F4, step 2.1, step 1.4]

Conclusion: steps 3.1 and 3.2 give $r=0$ and $r=1$ for the rank of any free chart at $(x)$, a contradiction; hence the finite-type coherent sheaf $\mathcal F=\widetilde{A/(x)}$ on the locally Noetherian scheme $X=\operatorname{Spec}k[x]$ is not locally free of finite rank at $(x)$, while by step 1.1 it is coherent of finite type. Its fibre dimension is $1$ at $(x)$ and $0$ at every other point, in particular at the generic point, so this fibre dimension is not locally constant and the false claim is refuted; finite type and coherence must be checked separately from local freeness. [step 1.1, step 2.2, step 2.3, step 3.1, step 3.2]

Choice accounting: the field $k$, the ring $A=k[x]$, the module $M=A/(x)$, the closed point $(x)$ and the generic point $(0)$ are fixed data, and no chart, generator family or isomorphism is selected by an infinite simultaneous choice; the only Axiom of Choice is the inherited one recorded in [F9], used through the associated-sheaf existence theorem and the closure description of [F7]. boundaries.evidence: The witness scheme $X=\operatorname{Spec}k[x]$ is nonempty: the closed point $(x)$ and the generic point $\eta=(0)$ both exist by step 1.1, and the fibre computed in step 2.1 is nonzero. The empty index boundary is therefore not part of this counterexample; over $X=\varnothing$ the false statement would be vacuous, and no witness could be extracted from it.

The module $M=A/(x)\cong k$ is nonzero by [F1] and step 1.1, so the zero sheaf is not the witness; the zero-module boundary appears only as the rank $r=0$, which step 3.1 derives from the vanishing fibre at the generic point, while by [F8] the sheaf $\mathcal O^0=0$ is the rank-zero free sheaf.

The rank-one case occurs at the closed point: step 3.2 shows that any free chart at $(x)$ has fibre $\kappa((x))^r$ of dimension $r$, while step 2.1 computes that fibre as one-dimensional over $\kappa((x))\cong k$, forcing $r=1$.

The degenerate point is the generic point $\eta=(0)$, whose maximal ideal is zero and whose local ring is the field $\kappa(\eta)=\operatorname{Frac}(A)$; steps 1.2 and 2.2 show $\mathcal F_\eta=0$ and $\mathcal F(\eta)=0$, and it is this degeneracy that step 3.1 uses to force $r=0$, contradicting step 3.2.

The only ordered parameter in the counterexample is the rank $r\ge0$, whose endpoint is $r=0$; step 3.1 realises the endpoint by deriving $r=0$ from the vanishing fibre at the generic point, and [F8] records $\mathcal O^0=0$. No interval, degree or index endpoint occurs, since the example is the single affine line $\operatorname{Spec}k[x]$ with the single module $A/(x)$.

Step 5.1 records that the field $k$, the ring $k[x]$, the module $A/(x)$, the closed point $(x)$ and the generic point $(0)$ are fixed data and that no chart, generator family or isomorphism is selected by an infinite simultaneous choice; the only Axiom of Choice is the inherited one recorded in [F9]. The distinguished open $D(f)$ of step 2.3 is supplied by the refinement property [F6] for the single point $(x)$, not by a choice function.

The refused implication is the forward direction 'finite type (indeed coherent) implies locally free of finite rank'; its hypothesis is established in step 1.1, where $\mathcal F=\widetilde{A/(x)}$ is shown coherent of finite type on the locally Noetherian scheme $X$, and its conclusion is refuted in steps 2.3 to 4.1.

The converse implication 'locally free implies finite type' is true and is not attacked here: [F8] records that a locally free sheaf is quasi-coherent, and the item uses the local-freeness hypothesis only in step 2.3 to produce a chart $\mathcal F|_U\cong\mathcal O_U^r$ and to deduce the two incompatible ranks $r=0$ and $r=1$, so the failure is located in the direction displayed above.

boundaries.evidence: The witness is not empty: $X$ contains the two copies of $Y=\operatorname{Spec}A$, and $V$ contains every $D(x_j)$ and in particular the prime $\mathfrak p_F$ of step 1.2. The empty boundary is the case of the empty open subscheme, where gluing along $V=\varnothing$ would not identify anything and the section $(z,0)$ of step 3.2 would not be a section over a nonempty overlap; that degenerate gluing is excluded by $V\neq\varnothing$, shown in step 1.2.

The module $\mathcal F=\mathcal O_X$ is not the zero sheaf, and the pair $(z,0)$ of step 3.2 is a nonzero section because $z\neq0$ in $A_t$ by step 2.1; the zero module would have zero pushforward and would be quasi-coherent, so the zero boundary cannot witness the failure. The rank-zero aspect appears only in the second entry of the pair $(z,0)$.

With one copy of $Y$ instead of two the morphism is the identity of an affine scheme, which is quasi-compact and quasi-separated and whose pushforward of $\mathcal O_Y$ is quasi-coherent; the counterexample needs exactly two copies, whose intersection is $V$, as used in step 3.2 and in the non-quasi-separatedness of step 2.4. The index $j$ of step 1.2 is the least index outside a finite set, a one-element choice.

The degeneration excluded here is that of an empty or quasi-compact overlap: if $V$ were quasi-compact the gluing would be quasi-separated and the pushforward would be quasi-coherent by the theorem [F7]. Step 1.2 shows $V$ is non-quasi-compact by exhibiting the prime $\mathfrak p_F$ outside every member of a finite subfamily, so the degenerate quasi-compact-overlap case does not occur.

The tensor product adds the indices: fix $n,m\in\mathbb Z$ and write $e_0^{(n)}$ and $e_\infty^{(n)}$ for the frames of $\mathcal O(n)$, and similarly for $m$; by [F5] the tensor product $\mathcal O(n)\otimes\mathcal O(m)$ is free of rank one on $U_0$ with generator $g_0=e_0^{(n)}\otimes e_0^{(m)}$, and free of rank one on $U_\infty$ with generator $g_\infty=e_\infty^{(n)}\otimes e_\infty^{(m)}$. On $W$ the frame relations give $g_\infty=(t^ne_0^{(n)})\otimes(t^me_0^{(m)})=t^{n+m}g_0$, and inverting gives $g_0=t^{-(n+m)}g_\infty$, so the trivialisations of $\mathcal O(n)\otimes\mathcal O(m)$ on the two charts have exactly the overlap identification $e_\infty^{(n+m)}=t^{n+m}e_0^{(n+m)}$ that defines $\mathcal O(n+m)$ in [F1]; by the uniqueness clause of [F4] there is a canonical isomorphism $\mathcal O(n)\otimes\mathcal O(m)\cong\mathcal O(n+m)$ carrying $g_0$ to $e_0^{(n+m)}$ and $g_\infty$ to $e_\infty^{(n+m)}$. [F1, F4, F5, step 1.1]

The dual negates the index: since $\mathcal O(n)$ is invertible with the trivialisations determined by the frames $e_0$ and $e_\infty$, its dual $\mathcal O(n)^\vee$ is invertible and free of rank one on each chart with the dual frames $e_0^\vee$ and $e_\infty^\vee$ characterised by $e_0^\vee(e_0)=1$ and $e_\infty^\vee(e_\infty)=1$ [F2, F3]. On $W$ one has $e_\infty=t^ne_0$, hence $(t^{-n}e_0^\vee)(e_\infty)=t^{-n}e_0^\vee(t^ne_0)=t^{-n}t^n=1$, and since the dual is free of rank one there the section with this property is unique, so $e_\infty^\vee=t^{-n}e_0^\vee$; equivalently $e_0^\vee=t^ne_\infty^\vee$, which is the overlap identification defining $\mathcal O(-n)$ in [F1], so the uniqueness clause of [F4] gives a canonical isomorphism $\mathcal O(n)^\vee\cong\mathcal O(-n)$ carrying $e_0^\vee$ to the frame of $\mathcal O(-n)$ on $U_0$ and $e_\infty^\vee$ to its frame on $U_\infty$. [F1, F2, F3, F4, step 1.1]

[F1, F2, F3, F6, step 1.1, step 2.1, step 2.2] ∎

degree-$d$ parts $(\operatorname{Sym}^d_A(M))^{\sim}$ glue to sheaves
$\operatorname{Sym}^d(\mathcal F)$ with
$$\operatorname{Sym}(\mathcal F)=\bigoplus_{d\ge0}\operatorname{Sym}^d(\mathcal F), \qquad \operatorname{Sym}^0(\mathcal F)=\mathcal O_X,\qquad \operatorname{Sym}^1(\mathcal F)=\mathcal F ,$$
the direct sum being taken in the category of $\mathcal O_X$-modules; on an
affine chart it corresponds under the equivalence $N\mapsto\widetilde N$ to the
direct sum of the modules $\operatorname{Sym}^d_A(M)$
([[thm-affine-quasi-coherent-equivalence]]), and degreewise gluing is
legitimate because restriction isomorphisms are degree-preserving. The
multiplication of the affine models induces multiplication maps
$\operatorname{Sym}^d(\mathcal F)\otimes_{\mathcal O_X}
\operatorname{Sym}^e(\mathcal F)\to\operatorname{Sym}^{d+e}(\mathcal F)$,
so $\operatorname{Sym}(\mathcal F)$ is generated as an $\mathcal O_X$-algebra
by its degree-one part $\mathcal F$, local sections of $\mathcal F$ commute in
$\operatorname{Sym}(\mathcal F)$, and the degree-$d$ piece is the quotient of
the $d$-fold tensor power $\mathcal F^{\otimes d}$
([[def-sheaf-tensor-product]]) by the local relations
$v_1\otimes\cdots\otimes v_d=v_{\sigma(1)}\otimes\cdots\otimes v_{\sigma(d)}$
for all permutations $\sigma$; the tensor powers are quasi-coherent with
$(\mathcal F^{\otimes d})|_U\cong(M^{\otimes_Ad})^{\sim}$ by iteration of
[[lem-tensor-qc-modules-quasi-coherent]]. Equivalently,
$\operatorname{Sym}(\mathcal F)$ is obtained from the tensor-algebra
presentation of $\mathcal F$ by imposing the local relations
$v\otimes w=w\otimes v$.

[F1]

The symmetric algebra. $\operatorname{Sym}(0)$ has $\operatorname{Sym}^0(0)=\mathcal O_X$ and $\operatorname{Sym}^1(0)=0$ and is generated in degree one; hence all its positive graded parts vanish and $\operatorname{Sym}(0)=\mathcal O_X$ with degree-one part $0$, the case $r=0$ of $\operatorname{Sym}(\mathcal O_X^r)=\mathcal O_X[T_1,\dots,T_r]$. [F3]

The total space. The dual of the zero module is again $0$, so $\mathbb V(0)=\operatorname{Spec}_X\operatorname{Sym}(0)=\operatorname{Spec}_X\mathcal O_X$; on an affine chart $U=\operatorname{Spec}R\subseteq X$ the relative spectrum of $\mathcal O_X$ has $\pi^{-1}(U)=\operatorname{Spec}\Gamma(U,\mathcal O_X)=\operatorname{Spec}R=U$, with the identity transition maps on inclusions, so the glued structure morphism is the identity of $X$ and $\mathbb V(0)=X$. [F2, F4]

Rank. The relative coordinate algebra of $\mathbb V(0)$ is $\mathcal O_X$ with degree-one part $(\mathcal O_X)_1=0=\mathcal O_X^0$, so the rank function of this geometric vector bundle is identically $0$, and dually its sheaf of sections is $0^\vee=0$. [F2, F3]

Fibres. Since the structure morphism of $\mathbb V(0)$ is the identity, the preimage of a point $x\in X$ is the one-point set $\{x\}$: the fibre of the bundle contains exactly one point, the zero vector, above $x$. On the module side the fibre of $0$ at $x$ is $0(x)=0_x\otimes_{\mathcal O_{X,x}}\kappa(x)=0$, the zero $\kappa(x)$-vector space with exactly one element, so the geometric and linear descriptions of the rank-zero fibre agree. [F5, step 1.3]

By [F2] and [F3], the stalk of the tensor pullback is $$(g^*(\widetilde M))_{\mathfrak q}\cong(O_U)_{\mathfrak q}\otimes_{(g^{-1}\mathcal O_V)_{\mathfrak q}}(g^{-1}\widetilde M)_{\mathfrak q}\cong B_{\mathfrak q}\otimes_{A_{\mathfrak p}}\widetilde M_{\mathfrak p}\cong B_{\mathfrak q}\otimes_{A_{\mathfrak p}}M_{\mathfrak p},$$ while by [F2] and [F3] the stalk of the associated sheaf is $$\widetilde{(B\otimes_AM)}_{\mathfrak q}\cong(B\otimes_AM)_{\mathfrak q}\cong B_{\mathfrak q}\otimes_{A_{\mathfrak p}}M_{\mathfrak p};$$ the map $\delta_{\mathfrak q}$ is $B_{\mathfrak q}$-linear and sends the class of $1\otimes m$ to the class of $1\otimes m$ under these identifications, and since the elements $1\otimes m$ generate $B_{\mathfrak q}\otimes_{A_{\mathfrak p}}M_{\mathfrak p}$ as a $B_{\mathfrak q}$-module, $\delta_{\mathfrak q}$ is the canonical isomorphism between the two copies of $B_{\mathfrak q}\otimes_{A_{\mathfrak p}}M_{\mathfrak p}$. [F2, F3, step 1.2]

3.1 The affine isomorphism: a morphism of sheaves of modules is an isomorphism if and only if its stalk maps are isomorphisms, so step 2.1 shows that $\delta$ is an isomorphism of $\mathcal O_U$-modules; hence $g^*(\widetilde M)\cong\widetilde{(B\otimes_AM)}$ and, by step 1.1, $f^*\mathcal F|_U\cong\widetilde{(B\otimes_AM)}$. This proves the affine form (2), and it shows that for every admissible pair $(U,V)$ the restriction of $f^*\mathcal F$ to the affine open $U$ is an associated sheaf, hence quasi-coherent on $U$ by [F4]. [F4, F8, step 1.1, step 2.1]

Global quasi-coherence: let $x\in X$. Choose an affine open $U_0=\operatorname{Spec}B_0\subseteq X$ containing $x$; since $\mathcal F$ is quasi-coherent there are an affine open $V=\operatorname{Spec}A\subseteq Y$ containing $f(x)$ and an $A$-module $M$ with $\mathcal F|_V\cong\widetilde M$. The set $U_0\cap f^{-1}(V)$ is an open neighbourhood of $x$ in $U_0$, so by [F5] it contains a distinguished open $D(b)$ with $x\in D(b)$; the open $D(b)=\operatorname{Spec}(B_0)_b$ is affine, maps into $V$, and satisfies $\mathcal F|_V\cong\widetilde M$. Therefore the family of all affine opens $U\subseteq X$ that admit an affine open $V\subseteq Y$ with $f(U)\subseteq V$ and $\mathcal F|_V\cong\widetilde M$ covers $X$, and each member has $f^*\mathcal F|_U$ associated by step 3.1; by the affine cover criterion [F4], $f^*\mathcal F$ is quasi-coherent. This proves (1). [F4, F5, step 3.1]

Choice accounting: the cover used in step 4.1 is the family of all admissible affine opens, which is determined by the data, so no chart, module or isomorphism is selected; the comparison morphism $\delta$ of step 1.2 is built from the canonical class maps of the inverse image colimit, and the identifications of step 2.1 are the canonical stalk and localisation isomorphisms. Hence the only use of the Axiom of Choice is the inherited one recorded in the Statement through [F7]. [F7, step 1.2, step 2.1, step 4.1] ∎

Step 5.1 records the accounting: the family of all admissible affine opens is used as a cover, so no chart, module or isomorphism is selected, and the construction of $\delta$ in step 1.2 and the stalk identifications of step 2.1 are canonical; the only Axiom of Choice is the inherited one from the associated-sheaf and affine-equivalence machinery recorded in [F7].

Forward, quasi-coherence of the pullback: by step 3.1 every member $U$ of the admissible affine cover has $f^*\mathcal F|_U\cong\widetilde{(B\otimes_AM)}$, an associated sheaf; applying the affine cover criterion in step 4.1 then gives that $f^*\mathcal F$ is quasi-coherent.

derivations.claim: Universal property of the affine model: for a commutative ring $A$, an $A$-module $M$ and a commutative $A$-algebra $C$, the map $g\mapsto g\circ\eta$ induced by the degree-one inclusion $\eta:M\to\operatorname{Sym}_A(M)$ is a bijection $A\text{-}\mathrm{Alg}(\operatorname{Sym}_A(M),C)\to\operatorname{Hom}_A(M,C)$: apply the universal property of [F1] on $X=\operatorname{Spec}A$ to $\mathcal F=\widetilde M$ and the sheaf of commutative $\mathcal O_X$-algebras $\widetilde C$, and translate along the affine equivalence [F2], under which $\mathcal O_X$-linear maps $\widetilde M\to\widetilde C$ are the $A$-linear maps $M\to C$, while $\operatorname{Sym}(\widetilde M)\cong(\operatorname{Sym}_A(M))^{\sim}$ by the affine model of [F1] and the tensor identifications [F3] match the multiplications, so $\mathcal O_X$-algebra maps $\operatorname{Sym}(\widetilde M)\to\widetilde C$ are the $A$-algebra maps $\operatorname{Sym}_A(M)\to C$; the bijection is natural in $C$ because the equivalence and the universal property are. [F1, F2, F3]

2.1 Base change of the affine model: for a ring map $A\to B$ and an $A$-module $M$ there is a canonical isomorphism of graded $B$-algebras $\beta:B\otimes_A\operatorname{Sym}_A(M)\to\operatorname{Sym}_B(B\otimes_AM)$ characterized by $\beta(1\otimes\eta_A(m))=\eta_B(1\otimes m)$: both sides represent the same functor of commutative $B$-algebras, since [F6] identifies $B$-algebra maps $B\otimes_A\operatorname{Sym}_A(M)\to D$ with $A$-algebra maps $\operatorname{Sym}_A(M)\to D$, step 1.1 with $A$-linear maps $M\to D$, [F6] with $B$-linear maps $B\otimes_AM\to D$, and step 1.1 over $B$ with $B$-algebra maps $\operatorname{Sym}_B(B\otimes_AM)\to D$; the identity of $\operatorname{Sym}_B(B\otimes_AM)$ corresponds to a map $\beta$ and the identity of $B\otimes_A\operatorname{Sym}_A(M)$ to a map $\gamma$, and naturality in $D$ gives $\beta\circ\gamma=\mathrm{id}$ and $\gamma\circ\beta=\mathrm{id}$. Under this correspondence $\beta$ is the unique $B$-algebra map with $\beta(1\otimes\eta_A(m))=\eta_B(1\otimes m)$, so it preserves the degree-one generators and hence the grading, and for $A\to B\to C$ both composites $C\otimes_A\operatorname{Sym}_A(M)\to\operatorname{Sym}_C(C\otimes_AM)$ in the claim are $C$-algebra maps sending $1\otimes\eta_A(m)$ to $\eta_C(1\otimes m)$; since the source is generated as a $C$-algebra by these elements, the composites agree, the identifications $C\otimes_B(B\otimes_AN)\cong C\otimes_AN$ being those of [F6]. Restriction to open subschemes: for an open subscheme $W\subseteq X$ there is a canonical isomorphism of graded $\mathcal O_W$-algebras $\operatorname{Sym}(\mathcal F)|_W\cong\operatorname{Sym}(\mathcal F|_W)$, compatible with inclusions $W'\subseteq W$: the affine opens $U=\operatorname{Spec}A\subseteq W$ with $\mathcal F|_U\cong\widetilde M$ cover $W$ because $\mathcal F$ is quasi-coherent, and on each of them $\operatorname{Sym}(\mathcal F)|_U\cong(\operatorname{Sym}_A(M))^{\sim}$ by the affine model, while applying the same model to the quasi-coherent sheaf $\mathcal F|_W$ on $W$ gives $\operatorname{Sym}(\mathcal F|_W)|_U\cong(\operatorname{Sym}_A(M))^{\sim}$ with the same module $M=\Gamma(U,\mathcal F)$; for affine $U'\subseteq U$ both identifications restrict by the canonical base-change isomorphism of step 2.1 for the ring map $\Gamma(U,\mathcal O)\to\Gamma(U',\mathcal O)$, so the chartwise isomorphisms agree on overlaps and glue by [F5] to a graded $\mathcal O_W$-algebra isomorphism, and passing to the subcover inside $W'\subseteq W$ shows compatibility with inclusions. [F1, F5, step 2.1]

boundaries.evidence: The statement compares finite type with coherence over arbitrary bases; the empty scheme and the zero module are unproblematic, since the zero sheaf is coherent and of finite type by the definition, and the example witnessing the failure is the structure sheaf of a nonempty, nonzero spectrum.

The zero module satisfies both sides of the distinction, being coherent and of finite type by the statement of the definition; the warning in this remark concerns nonzero, indeed locally free, examples such as the module $A$ of the definition's example, so it does not rest on any behaviour of zero objects.

The example in the definition is the free module of rank one $A$ over the non-Noetherian ring $A$, that is the case of a single generator; it is finitely presented yet admits an endomorphism with non-finitely-generated kernel, which is exactly the unit-rank case in which the coherence test fails.

The degenerate instances are the point of the remark: the base ring $A$ of the example is non-Noetherian and non-reduced, its ideal of relations is not finitely generated, and the module in question is free of finite rank; the statement of the remark is that in this degeneracy the implication from finite presentation (or finite local freeness) to coherence fails.

The endpoints of the coherence test are the finite ranks $n=0$ and $n=1$ of the test morphism; the trivial test with $n=0$ has zero kernel and is unproblematic, while the example uses the extreme nonzero case $n=1$ of an endomorphism of the structure sheaf, where the kernel condition already fails.

The remark introduces no selection at all: the ring, the module $A$ and the endomorphism of the example are explicit, and the cited theorem and definition are invoked only for their statements. The Axiom of Choice enters only as inherited by the coherence theory through the theorem cited in the statement, with no new choice principle used.

The direction that survives is the statement of the theorem: on a locally Noetherian scheme finite type implies coherence, hence coherent and finite type coincide there; the remark explicitly restricts that implication to locally Noetherian bases and warns that its hypothesis is used essentially.

The direction that fails is the reverse one: without the locally Noetherian hypothesis, finite type (even finite presentation and finite local freeness) does not imply coherence. The counterexample is the rank-one free module $A$ of the definition's example on the non-Noetherian spectrum $X=\operatorname{Spec}A$, whose structure sheaf carries a morphism with non-finitely-generated kernel, so it is not coherent there.

The only $A$-module is $0$, whose associated sheaf is the zero sheaf on the empty space, and the only sheaf on $\varnothing$ is the zero sheaf, so $M\mapsto\widetilde M$ and $\Gamma$ are the identity functors between the one-object, one-morphism categories and each claim holds. Each point has a basic neighbourhood on which $\mathcal F$ is associated to its own sections: let $x\in X$; by [F1] there are an affine open $V=\operatorname{Spec}B\subseteq X$ containing $x$ and a $B$-module $N$ with $\mathcal F|_V\cong\widetilde N$; by [F2] choose $f\in A$ with $x\in D(f)\subseteq V$. In $V=\operatorname{Spec}B$ the open $D(f)$ is the distinguished open cut out by the image of $f$ in $B$, with ring of sections $A_f$; applying [F5] to the affine open subscheme $D(f)=\operatorname{Spec}A_f$ of $V$ gives $(\widetilde N)|_{D(f)}\cong\widetilde{(A_f\otimes_BN)}$. Restricting the isomorphism $\mathcal F|_V\cong\widetilde N$ therefore yields $\mathcal F|_{D(f)}\cong\widetilde{(A_f\otimes_BN)}$, and by [F6] applied to the ring $A_f$ and the $A_f$-module $A_f\otimes_BN$ this module is $\Gamma(D(f),\mathcal F)$. Hence $$\mathcal F|_{D(f)}\;\cong\;\widetilde{\Gamma(D(f),\mathcal F)}$$ for such an $f$. [F1, F2, F5, F6]

The unit and naturality: claim 1 is the case $f=1$ of the canonical identification $\Gamma(D(f),\widetilde M)\cong M_f$ of [F6], which is natural in $M$: an $A$-linear map $u:M\to N$ makes the square with the unit maps commute because $\widetilde u_X=u$ under these identifications. Hence $\Gamma(X,-)\circ(-)^{\sim}\cong\mathrm{id}_{\operatorname{Mod}_A}$. [F6]

Full faithfulness: let $M,N$ be $A$-modules. If $\psi:\widetilde M\to \widetilde N$ is a morphism of $\mathcal O_X$-modules, put $u=\psi_X:M\to N$ under the identifications $\Gamma(X,\widetilde M)=M$, $\Gamma(X,\widetilde N)=N$ of [F6]. With $M$ and $N$ finitely generated, $P$ is finitely generated: lift finitely many generators of $N$ to $P$ and add generators of $M$ [F4]. Therefore $\mathcal E|_V$ is of finite type on every chart of the cover, so $\mathcal E$ is of finite type [F2]; being quasi-coherent by hypothesis, $\mathcal E$ is coherent by step 2.1. The identity morphism $\varphi=\mathrm{id}_{\mathcal F}$ has kernel $0$, image $\mathcal F$ and cokernel $0$, so step 3.1 returns the coherent modules $0$ and $\mathcal F$ as expected; the test map $\tau:\mathcal O_U^n\to\mathcal F|_U$ in claim (1) is allowed to be the identity when $\mathcal F=\mathcal O_X$ and $U=X$, with kernel $0$ of finite type, and step 2.1 covers every test map including this one.

The hypotheses are sharp and are the degenerate instances: over a non-Noetherian affine base the kernel of a map of finitely generated modules need not be finitely generated, and the example inside [[def-coherent-module-scheme]] shows a finitely presented quasi-coherent module that is not coherent, so the local Noetherian hypothesis of the statement is used exactly in step 2.1 through [F4]; the zero ring gives the empty spectrum, handled by the empty case.

The numerical extremes in claim (1) are $n=0$, where $\tau:\mathcal O_U^0=0\to\mathcal F|_U$ is the zero map with kernel $\widetilde{(\ker\psi)}$ for $\psi:B^0=0\to N$, a finitely generated module, so step 2.1 applies unchanged; the rank extremes of claim (2) are the zero module and the free modules $\mathcal O_X^n$, coherent by step 2.1, and the extreme exact sequences of claim (3) are $0\to0\to\mathcal E\to\mathcal E\to0$ and $0\to\mathcal F\to\mathcal F\to0\to0$, handled by step 3.2.

Step 5.1 records the accounting: only finite subcovers of the given Noetherian affine charts, finite generating families and the isomorphism supplied by the affine equivalence are used, and no simultaneous selection over an infinite family is made, so the only Axiom of Choice is the inherited one recorded in [F11] with dependency [[def-axiom-of-choice]].
Forward in claim (1): coherent means quasi-coherent of finite type by the definition of coherence [F1], which is step 1.3.

Reverse in claim (1): if $\mathcal F$ is quasi-coherent of finite type, then on each Noetherian affine chart of step 1.1 the module $N$ is finitely generated by step 1.2 and the kernel of any $\psi:B^n\to N$ is finitely generated by [F4], so the kernel sheaf is of finite type; step 2.1 globalises this to the coherence test over all opens $U$ and all $\tau$, using that the charts $D(f)=\operatorname{Spec}A_f$ have Noetherian coordinate rings by [F5].

risk_review.notes: Checked that every point of an open admits a Noetherian distinguished affine neighbourhood. Finite type QC modules are finitely generated on each affine chart; Noetherianity then makes kernels of finite-free maps finite type, giving coherence. Exact localization and affine equivalence give coherent kernels, images, cokernels, finite sums and extensions. The Noetherian hypothesis is essential; zero objects and n=0 relation maps are covered. AC is inherited through QC interfaces.

derivations.claim: The fibre of a presented module: let $U=\operatorname{Spec}A$ be an affine open with $\mathcal F|_U\cong\widetilde M$ for a finitely generated $A$-module $M$, and fix a presentation $A^{(J)}\xrightarrow{\varphi}A^n\to M\to0$ with $n$ finite; for $\mathfrak p\in U$ the localisation and the tensor product with $\kappa(\mathfrak p)=A_{\mathfrak p}/\mathfrak pA_{\mathfrak p}$ give the exact sequence $\kappa(\mathfrak p)^{(J)}\xrightarrow{\varphi\otimes\kappa(\mathfrak p)}\kappa(\mathfrak p)^n\to M\otimes_A\kappa(\mathfrak p)\to0$, and $\mathcal F(\mathfrak p)=M_{\mathfrak p}\otimes_{A_{\mathfrak p}}\kappa(\mathfrak p)=M\otimes_A\kappa(\mathfrak p)$; hence, with $\varphi$ also denoting its reduced matrix, $\dim_{\kappa(\mathfrak p)}\mathcal F(\mathfrak p)=n-\operatorname{rank}(\varphi\otimes\kappa(\mathfrak p))$. [F3, F6, F7, F8]

Minors detect the rank drop: for a given $r\ge0$ and $s=n-r$, the inequality $\operatorname{rank}(\varphi\otimes\kappa(\mathfrak p))<s$ holds if and only if all $s\times s$ minors of the reduced matrix vanish, which happens if and only if every $s\times s$ minor of the matrix of $\varphi$ lies in $\mathfrak p$, that is, $I_{n-r}(\varphi)\subseteq\mathfrak p$; the conventions of [F1] give $I_{n-r}(\varphi)=A$ when $s\le0$, and $\operatorname{rank}<s$ is then impossible, while for $s>n$ one has $I_{n-r}(\varphi)=0$ and $\operatorname{rank}<s$ holds always. [F1, F9, step 1.1]

The rank locus on a chart: combining steps 1.1 and 2.1, for $\mathfrak p\in U$ one has $\dim_{\kappa(\mathfrak p)}\mathcal F(\mathfrak p)>r$ if and only if $I_{n-r}(\varphi)\subseteq\mathfrak p$; by [F1] the stalk of $\operatorname{Fitt}_r(\mathcal F)$ at $\mathfrak p$ is $I_{n-r}(\varphi)\cdot A_{\mathfrak p}$, and $I\cdot A_{\mathfrak p}\subseteq\mathfrak pA_{\mathfrak p}$ if and only if $I\subseteq\mathfrak p$; hence $\mathfrak p\in V(\operatorname{Fitt}_r(\mathcal F))$ if and only if $\dim_{\kappa(\mathfrak p)}\mathcal F(\mathfrak p)>r$. [F1, step 1.1, step 2.1]

Converse, the case $n=r$: let $U=\operatorname{Spec}A$ be affine with $\mathcal F|_U\cong\widetilde M$, presentation $A^{(J)}\xrightarrow{\varphi}A^n\to M\to0$, and assume $I_{n-r}(\varphi)=A$, $I_{n-r+1}(\varphi)=0$ for some $r\ge1$. If $A=0$ the conclusion is vacuous, so assume $A\neq0$; then $n\ge r$, since $n-r+1\le0$ would force $A=I_{n-r+1}(\varphi)=0$. If $n=r$, then $I_1(\varphi)=I_{n-r+1}(\varphi)=0$ says that every entry of the matrix of $\varphi$ is zero, so $\varphi=0$ and $M=\operatorname{coker}\varphi\cong A^n=A^r$ is free of rank $r$. [F1, step 2.1]

Claim 1 globally: the affine charts of step 3.1 cover $X$ by [F2] and the assertion is pointwise in each chart, so $V(\operatorname{Fitt}_r(\mathcal F))=\{x:\dim_{\kappa(x)}\mathcal F(x)>r\}$ and $D(\operatorname{Fitt}_r(\mathcal F))$ is its complement $\{x:\dim_{\kappa(x)}\mathcal F(x)\le r\}$; this proves claim 1. [F2, step 3.1]

Converse, the case $n>r$: keep the hypotheses of step 3.2 with $s=n-r\ge1$. The $s\times s$ minors of $\varphi$ generate $I_s(\varphi)=A$, so the distinguished opens $D(\delta)\subseteq\operatorname{Spec}A$, as $\delta$ runs over the $s\times s$ minors, cover $\operatorname{Spec}A$; fix such a minor $\delta$ and invert it. Over $A_\delta$ the selected minor is a unit, so after permuting the $s$ chosen rows and columns into the top-left corner, row operations by invertible $n\times n$ matrices and column operations by an automorphism of $A_\delta^{(J)}$ put the matrix of $\varphi\otimes A_\delta$ into block form $\begin{pmatrix}I_s&0\\ C&\psi\end{pmatrix}$ with $\psi$ of size $r$ rows; the $(s+1)\times(s+1)$ minors formed from $s$ rows and $s$ columns of the identity block together with one further row and column are, up to sign, exactly the entries of $\psi$, and they vanish because $I_{s+1}(\varphi)\otimes A_\delta=I_{n-r+1}(\varphi)\otimes A_\delta=0$; hence $\psi=0$ and $M_\delta\cong\operatorname{coker}\begin{pmatrix}I_s&0\\ C&0\end{pmatrix}\cong A_\delta^{\,r}$, because the image is the graph $\{(x,Cx)\}$, a direct summand of $A_\delta^n$ of rank $s$. Thus $\mathcal F$ is free of rank $r$ on each member $D(\delta)$ of a cover of $U$, so $\mathcal F|_U$ is locally free of rank $r$. [F1, F9, step 3.2]

Claim 2, the support: taking $r=0$ in claim 1 gives $V(\operatorname{Fitt}_0(\mathcal F))=\{x:\dim_{\kappa(x)}\mathcal F(x)>0\}=\{x:\mathcal F(x)
eq0\}$. For finite type $\mathcal F$ one has $\mathcal F(x)=0$ only if $\mathcal F$ vanishes on a neighbourhood of $x$, hence only if $\mathcal F_x=0$, and conversely $\mathcal F_x=0$ gives $\mathcal F(x)=0$; therefore $\{x:\mathcal F(x)
eq0\}=\{x:\mathcal F_x
eq0\}=\operatorname{Supp}(\mathcal F)$, and this agrees with the closedness of the support in [F5]. [F4, F5, step 4.1]

Claim 3, the locally free case: suppose $\mathcal F$ is finite locally free of rank $r$, so that by [F2] $X$ is covered by affine opens $U=\operatorname{Spec}A$ with $\mathcal F|_U\cong\mathcal O_U^r=\widetilde{A^r}$; for the presentation $A^r=A^r$ with $n=r$ generators and no relations the matrix has $r$ rows and $0$ columns, so by the conventions of [F1] $I_{r-k}(\varphi)=A$ for $k\ge r$ and $I_{r-k}(\varphi)=0$ for $0\le k<r$, whence $\operatorname{Fitt}_k(\mathcal F)|_U=\mathcal O_U$ for $k\ge r$ and $=0$ for $k<r$; in particular $\operatorname{Fitt}_{r-1}(\mathcal F)|_U=0$ and $\operatorname{Fitt}_r(\mathcal F)|_U=\mathcal O_U$ for every member of a cover of $X$, and since membership in an ideal subsheaf and the equality with $\mathcal O_X$ are checked on a cover, $\operatorname{Fitt}_{r-1}(\mathcal F)=0$ and $\operatorname{Fitt}_r(\mathcal F)=\mathcal O_X$. [F1, F2, step 4.1]

Claim 4 globally: let $U\subseteq X$ be open with $\operatorname{Fitt}_{r-1}(\mathcal F)|_U=0$ and $\operatorname{Fitt}_r(\mathcal F)|_U=\mathcal O_U$. If $r=0$, claim 1 gives $\dim_{\kappa(x)}\mathcal F(x)\le0$, hence $\mathcal F(x)=0$, for every $x\in U$, and [F4] then shows that $\mathcal F$ vanishes on a neighbourhood of every point of $U$, so that $\mathcal F|_U=0$ is locally free of rank $0$. If $r\ge1$, cover $U$ by affine charts $V=\operatorname{Spec}A$ with $\mathcal F|_V\cong\widetilde M$; on each chart the restriction of the hypotheses reads $I_{n-r}(\varphi)=A$ and $I_{n-r+1}(\varphi)=0$ by [F1], so steps 3.2 and 4.2 show that $\mathcal F|_V$ is free of rank $r$ on the members of a cover of $V$; these covers for all charts combine to a cover of $U$ by opens on which $\mathcal F$ is free of rank $r$. This proves claim 4. [F1, F2, F4, step 3.2, step 4.2]

Claim 5, sharpness: let $k$ be a field, $A=k[t]/(t^2)$ with class $\varepsilon$ of $t$, so that $\varepsilon^2=0$ and $\varepsilon\neq0$, and let $M=A/(\varepsilon)=k$; then $M$ is generated by one element with the single relation $\varepsilon\cdot1=0$, giving a presentation $A\xrightarrow{\ \varepsilon\ }A\to M\to0$, and $\mathcal F=\widetilde M$ is a finite type quasi-coherent module on $X=\operatorname{Spec}A$, whose underlying space is the single point $\mathfrak p=(\varepsilon)$. The fibre there is $\mathcal F(\mathfrak p)=M\otimes_A\kappa(\mathfrak p)=M/\varepsilon M=k$, of dimension $1$ over $\kappa(\mathfrak p)=k$; the Fitting ideals of this presentation are $\operatorname{Fitt}_0(M)=I_1(\varphi)=(\varepsilon)\neq A$ and $\operatorname{Fitt}_1(M)=I_0(\varphi)=A$. Hence the equality $\operatorname{Fitt}_{r-1}(\mathcal F)=0$ fails for $r=1$ at every point, so by claim 4 the module is not locally free of rank $1$; directly, $\mathcal F\cong\mathcal O_X$ would give $M\cong\Gamma(X,\mathcal O_X)=A$, impossible because $\dim_kM=1$ while $\dim_kA=2$. This proves claim 5 and shows that the two Fitting equalities, not merely the pointwise fibre dimension, are needed for local freeness. [F1, F10, step 5.2, step 5.3]

Conclusion and choice accounting: claims 1 and 2 are steps 4.1 and 5.1, claim 3 is step 5.2, claim 4 is step 5.3 and claim 5 is step 6.1. All constructions are local and finite: a presentation with finitely many generators is used on one affine chart at a time, the minors of a matrix are indexed by finite subsets of that presentation, and the cover $\{D(\delta)\}$ in step 4.2 is the set of all distinguished opens defined by the minors, so no selection of points, presentations or minors is made; the only use of the Axiom of Choice is the one inherited from the associated-sheaf machinery through [F1] and [F5], and no Noetherian hypothesis is used, exactly as claimed. [F1, F5, step 4.1, step 5.1, step 5.2, step 5.3, step 6.1] ∎

boundaries.evidence: For $X=\varnothing$ every sheaf of modules is zero: step 4.1 gives $V(\operatorname{Fitt}_r)= \varnothing = \{x:\dim\mathcal F(x)>r\}$ and $D(\operatorname{Fitt}_r)=\varnothing$, step 5.1 gives $V(\operatorname{Fitt}_0)=\varnothing=\operatorname{Supp}(\mathcal F)$, and claims 3 and 4 are vacuous on a space with no points, the zero sheaf being locally free of rank $0$ everywhere.

For $\mathcal F=0$ the definition gives $\operatorname{Fitt}_k(\mathcal F)=\mathcal O_X$ for all $k\ge0$ and $\operatorname{Fitt}_{-1}=0$; then $V(\operatorname{Fitt}_r)=V(\mathcal O_X)=\varnothing=\{x:\dim0>r\}$ by step 4.1, $V(\operatorname{Fitt}_0)=\varnothing=\operatorname{Supp}(0)$ by step 5.1, and claim 3 holds since the zero sheaf is locally free of rank $0$ with $\operatorname{Fitt}_0=\mathcal O_X$ (step 5.2); claim 4 for $r=0$ is the vanishing branch of step 5.3.

For $\mathcal F=\mathcal O_X$ one has $\operatorname{Fitt}_0(\mathcal O_X)=0$ and $\operatorname{Fitt}_1(\mathcal O_X)=\mathcal O_X$ by step 5.2 with $r=1$, matching claim 3; the fibre has dimension $1$ at every point, so step 4.1 gives $V(\operatorname{Fitt}_1)=\varnothing=\{x:\dim>1\}$ and $V(\operatorname{Fitt}_0)=X=\{x:\dim>0\}$, and $r=1$ is the basic case of the converse in steps 3.2 and 4.2.

The theorem has no Noetherian, reduced or finiteness hypothesis beyond finite type, and the degenerate geometry is exactly what step 6.1 exercises: $A=k[t]/(t^2)$ is a non-reduced local ring and $M=A/(t)$ has fibre dimension $1$ at its only point but $\operatorname{Fitt}_0(M)=(t)\neq0$, so claim 4 fails for $r=1$; the cover $\{D(\delta)\}$ of step 4.2 is the set of all distinguished opens cut out by the minors, and no hypothesis of invertibility of a single global minor is made.

The parameter $r\ge0$ has the endpoint $r=0$, handled explicitly in step 5.1 (claim 2) and in the $r=0$ branch of step 5.3 for claim 4; the opposite extreme $r\ge n$, where $n$ is the number of generators on a chart, is absorbed by the conventions $I_m(\varphi)=A$ for $m\le0$ and $I_m(\varphi)=0$ above the number of rows recorded in step 2.1, so the equivalence $\dim>r\Leftrightarrow I_{n-r}(\varphi)\subseteq\mathfrak p$ remains correct at both ends, and $\operatorname{Fitt}_r=\mathcal O_X$ there.

Step 7.1 records the choice accounting: the only use of the Axiom of Choice is the one inherited from the associated-sheaf machinery through [F1] and [F5]; presentations are chosen one affine chart at a time with finitely many generators, minors are indexed by finite subsets of a given presentation, and the cover $\{D(\delta)\}$ in step 4.2 consists of *all* distinguished opens defined by the minors, so no point, presentation or minor is selected arbitrarily.

Forward: if $x\in V(\operatorname{Fitt}_r(\mathcal F))$ then $\dim_{\kappa(x)}\mathcal F(x)>r$. On a chart $I_{n-r}(\varphi)\subseteq\mathfrak p$ forces a rank drop and a fibre dimension exceeding $r$ by steps 1.1 and 2.1, and step 4.1 globalises this over the covering affine charts, including the trivial conventions at $n-r\le0$ and $n-r>n$.

Reverse: if $\dim_{\kappa(x)}\mathcal F(x)>r$ then $x\in V(\operatorname{Fitt}_r(\mathcal F))$ by step 4.1, and the genuinely converse direction of the theorem is that the *two* equalities $\operatorname{Fitt}_{r-1}=0$ and $\operatorname{Fitt}_r=\mathcal O_U$ force local freeness of rank $r$: step 3.2 covers $n=r$, step 4.2 inverts a unit minor to block-reduce the matrix for $n>r$, and step 5.3 globalises over a cover of $U$; step 6.1 shows the two equalities cannot be weakened to pointwise fibre dimension.

derivations.claim: The affine chart: let $U=\operatorname{Spec}A\subseteq X$ be affine with $\mathcal F|_U\cong\widetilde M$, $\mathcal G|_U\cong\widetilde N$, and let $u:M\to N$ be the $A$-linear map with $\varphi|_U$ corresponding to $\widetilde u$ under the full faithfulness of [F3]. The two sequences of $A$-modules $$0\longrightarrow\ker u\longrightarrow M\longrightarrow\operatorname{im}u\longrightarrow0,\qquad 0\longrightarrow\operatorname{im}u\longrightarrow N\longrightarrow\operatorname{coker}u\longrightarrow0$$ are exact, and localising them at a prime $\mathfrak p$ remains exact by [F4]; under the stalk identifications $(\widetilde M)_{\mathfrak p}=M_{\mathfrak p}$, $(\widetilde N)_{\mathfrak p}=N_{\mathfrak p}$ and $(\widetilde K)_{\mathfrak p}=K_{\mathfrak p}$ of [F5], and the naturality of these identifications, the stalk sequences of the sheaf maps $\widetilde{(\ker u)}\to\widetilde M\to\widetilde{(\operatorname{im}u)}$ and $\widetilde{(\operatorname{im}u)}\to\widetilde N\to\widetilde{(\operatorname{coker}u)}$ are exact at every prime, so by [F2] the sequences of $\mathcal O_U$-modules $$0\longrightarrow\widetilde{(\ker u)}\longrightarrow\widetilde M\xrightarrow{\ \widetilde u\ }\widetilde N\longrightarrow\widetilde{(\operatorname{coker}u)}\longrightarrow0$$ and the intermediate image sequence are exact. Consequently $\ker(\varphi|_U)\cong\widetilde{(\ker u)}$, $\operatorname{im}(\varphi|_U)\cong\widetilde{(\operatorname{im}u)}$ and $\operatorname{coker}(\varphi|_U)\cong\widetilde{(\operatorname{coker}u)}$ canonically. [F2, F3, F4, F5, given]

The affine isomorphisms are restrictions of the global sheaves: by the locality of [F1], restricting the global kernel, image and cokernel gives the kernel, image and cokernel of $\varphi|_U$; combined with step 1.1 this yields the three displayed isomorphisms of claim (1) on every affine open $U$ on which $\mathcal F$ and $\mathcal G$ are both associated. [F1, step 1.1]

The abelian subcategory: the zero sheaf is quasi-coherent, since it is $\widetilde 0$ on every affine chart, and the binary biproduct of quasi-coherent modules is quasi-coherent: on an affine chart with $\mathcal F|_U\cong\widetilde M$, $\mathcal G|_U\cong\widetilde N$ the objectwise direct sum has sections $\widetilde M(D(f))\oplus\widetilde N(D(f))=M_f\oplus N_f\cong(M\oplus N)_f$ on distinguished opens, compatibly with restriction by [F9], so it is $\widetilde{(M\oplus N)}$ on the covering family of common affine charts and hence quasi-coherent by [F6]. Since $\mathrm{Mod}(\mathcal O_X)$ is abelian by [F7] and $\operatorname{QCoh}(X)$ is a full subcategory closed under kernels, cokernels and finite biproducts computed in $\mathrm{Mod}(\mathcal O_X)$, the definition [F8] makes $\operatorname{QCoh}(X)$ an abelian subcategory and the inclusion a full additive exact embedding; images are kernels of cokernels, so they are covered as well. This is claim (2). [F6, F7, F8, F9, step 3.1]

No separation hypothesis: steps 1.1 to 4.1 use only affine charts, localisations, and the local definition of quasi-coherence; intersecting two affine charts and passing to a distinguished open is always possible in an affine scheme, and no statement about intersections of affine opens being affine, quasi-compactness or quasi-separatedness of $X$ is invoked. This is claim (3). [F6, step 3.1, step 4.1]

Choice accounting: the covering family used in steps 3.1 and 4.1 is the family of all affine opens on which the relevant sheaves are associated, which is determined by the data, so no chart or module is selected; the map $u$ of step 1.1 is the unique map corresponding to $\varphi|_U$ under the affine equivalence, and all identifications are the canonical ones of [F3] and [F5]. Hence the only use of the Axiom of Choice is the inherited one recorded in the Statement through [F10]. [F3, F5, F10, step 1.1, step 3.1, step 4.1] ∎

boundaries.evidence: For $X=\varnothing$ the only $\mathcal O_X$-modules are zero, so $\mathcal F=\mathcal G=0$, the map $\varphi$ is zero and $\ker\varphi=\operatorname{im}\varphi=\operatorname{coker}\varphi=0$ are quasi-coherent; step 3.1 applies with the empty affine cover, and step 4.1 gives that $\operatorname{QCoh}(\varnothing)$ is the zero abelian category.

For the zero map $\varphi=0:\mathcal F\to\mathcal G$ the corresponding map on an affine chart is $u=0:M\to N$, so $\ker u=M$, $\operatorname{im}u=0$ and $\operatorname{coker}u=N$; step 1.1 gives $\ker\varphi\cong\widetilde M=\mathcal F$, $\operatorname{im}\varphi=0$ and $\operatorname{coker}\varphi\cong\widetilde N=\mathcal G$, all quasi-coherent, and step 3.1 globalises.

For the identity $\varphi=\mathrm{id}_{\mathcal F}$ one has $u=\mathrm{id}_M$ on every affine chart, with $\ker u=0$, $\operatorname{im}u=M$ and $\operatorname{coker}u=0$; step 1.1 gives $\ker\varphi=0$, $\operatorname{im}\varphi\cong\mathcal F$ and $\operatorname{coker}\varphi=0$, the expected identities, and step 4.1 records that the zero sheaf and $\mathcal F$ are quasi-coherent.

The degenerate instances are non-Noetherian or non-reduced schemes, non-quasi-separated $X$, and arbitrary quasi-coherent modules that are not of finite type: step 1.1 applies the exactness of localisation to arbitrary $A$-modules $M,N$, step 3.1 intersects two affine charts and passes to a distinguished open, which needs only that the chart is affine, and step 5.1 records that no separatedness hypothesis is invoked; the modules $M,N$ need not be finitely generated.

The extreme morphisms of the statement are the zero map, covered by the zero row through step 1.1, and the identity, covered by the one row through step 1.1; there is no numerical or rank parameter with endpoints, and the module-level sequences of step 1.1 are the two extreme exact sequences $0\to M\xrightarrow{0}N\to N\to0$ and $0\to0\to M\xrightarrow{\mathrm{id}}M\to0$.

Step 6.1 records the accounting: the covering family used in steps 3.1 and 4.1 is the family of all affine opens on which the relevant sheaves are associated, so no chart or module is selected, and the map $u$ of step 1.1 is the unique map corresponding to $\varphi|_U$ under the affine equivalence; the only Axiom of Choice is the inherited one recorded in [F10].

Forward, from the closure properties to the abelian statement: steps 1.1 to 3.1 show that kernels, images and cokernels of morphisms of quasi-coherent modules are quasi-coherent, and step 4.1 adds the zero object and finite biproducts; by the definition of an abelian subcategory [F8] inside the abelian category $\mathrm{Mod}(\mathcal O_X)$ [F7], $\operatorname{QCoh}(X)$ is then an abelian subcategory.

Reverse, from the abelian statement to the concrete identifications: since $\operatorname{QCoh}(X)$ is a full subcategory closed under kernels and cokernels computed in $\mathrm{Mod}(\mathcal O_X)$ [F8], the kernel, image and cokernel of a morphism of quasi-coherent modules lie in $\operatorname{QCoh}(X)$; step 2.1 identifies them on each affine chart with $\widetilde{(\ker u)}$, $\widetilde{(\operatorname{im}u)}$ and $\widetilde{(\operatorname{coker}u)}$ of step 1.1, and step 3.1 globalises.

2.1 A surjection on an affine neighbourhood: choose a finite generating list of $M$. The kernel of $\psi$ is finitely generated. For a finite presentation $A^m\xrightarrow{\alpha}A^n\xrightarrow{\beta}N\to0$, form $P=\{(v,w):\psi(v)=\beta(w)\}$. The map on stalks is an isomorphism: let $\mathfrak q\subseteq B$ be the prime with $x=\mathfrak q$. If $r=0$ this says that the stalk vanishes, and $\mathcal F(\mathfrak p)=0$, so by [F3(i)] $\mathcal F$ vanishes on a neighbourhood of $x$ and $\mathcal F$ is free of rank $0$ there; assume $r\ge1$ from now on. [F5, F6, F3, step 3.1]

Killing the kernel: since $K$ is finitely generated and $K_{\mathfrak q}=0$, [F6(b)] gives $g\in B\setminus\mathfrak q$ with $K_g=0$; then $\psi_g:B_g^r\to N_g$ is surjective with zero kernel, hence an isomorphism. Restricting the isomorphism $\mathcal F|_V\cong\widetilde N$ to $D(g)$ and using [F7], $\mathcal F|_{D(g)}\cong\widetilde{(N_g)}\cong\widetilde{(B_g^r)}=\mathcal O_{D(g)}^r$, and $D(g)$ is an open neighbourhood of $x$ in $X$. Claims 1 and 2: the argument of steps 1.1, 2.1, 3.1, 4.1 and 5.1 applies to every $x\in Z_r(\mathcal F)$ and produces an open neighbourhood $D(g)$ of $x$ with $\mathcal F|_{D(g)}\cong\mathcal O_{D(g)}^r$; conversely, if $\mathcal F|_W\cong\mathcal O_W^r$ then $F_y\cong\mathcal O_{X,y}^r$ for every $y\in W$, so such a $W$ is contained in $Z_r(\mathcal F)$. Claim 3, sharpness: let $k$ be a field, $A=k[t]/(t^2)$ with class $\varepsilon$ of $t$, so that $\varepsilon^2=0$ and $\varepsilon

For $\mathcal F=0$ and $r=0$ one has $Z_0(\mathcal F)=X$ since every stalk is $0=\mathcal O_{X,x}^0$, claim 2 follows from $\mathcal F=\mathcal O_X^0$, and the vanishing branch of step 4.1 (where $\mathcal F(\mathfrak p)=0$) applies; for $r\ge1$ the locus $Z_r(\mathcal F)=\varnothing$ is open, and the zero module has no free stalk of positive rank.

For $r=1$ and $\mathcal F=\mathcal O_X$ every stalk is $\mathcal O_{X,x}^1$, so $Z_1(\mathcal F)=X$ is open, claim 2 holds with $V=X$, and the epimorphism of step 2.1 is the identity with kernel $K=0$ in step 3.1; for $\mathcal F=\mathcal O_X$ the example of step 7.1 does not occur because the kernel $\widetilde{(\varepsilon)}$ is nonzero.

The degenerate case is step 7.1: $A=k[t]/(t^2)$ is non-reduced and its unique point has fibre dimension $1$ while the stalk $k$ is not free, so the hypothesis of the theorem (a free stalk, i.e. vanishing of the kernel at the point) genuinely fails there; the positive proof never uses reducedness or Noetherianness, since step 3.1 only uses finite presentation to make the kernel finitely generated, and step 5.1 then inverts one element.

The only numerical parameter is $r\ge0$; its endpoint $r=0$ is handled by the vanishing branch of step 4.1, where $\mathcal F(\mathfrak p)=0$ forces $\mathcal F$ to vanish on a neighbourhood by Nakayama [F3(i)], and the opposite extreme consists of $r$ so large that $Z_r(\mathcal F)=\varnothing$, which is open and for which claim 2 is vacuous, so the equivalence of step 6.1 remains correct at both ends.

Step 8.1 records the accounting: the $r$ basis lifts of step 2.1, the finitely many generators of $K$ in step 3.1, and the finitely many denominators of step 5.1 are all finite choices; the only Axiom of Choice used is the one inherited from the associated-sheaf machinery of [F1] and [F7], and no point, chart or generating set is selected by an infinite choice.

Forward: if $x\in Z_r(\mathcal F)$, i.e. the stalk is free of rank $r$, then steps 2.1 to 5.1 construct an affine neighbourhood $V$ and an epimorphism $\varphi:\mathcal O_V^r\to\mathcal F|_V$ whose kernel is finitely generated (3.1) and whose localisation at $x$ is an isomorphism because a surjective map of free rank-$r$ modules over the local ring is injective (4.1), so after inverting one element the kernel dies and $\mathcal F|_{D(g)}\cong\mathcal O_{D(g)}^r$ (5.1); step 6.1 promotes this to the openness of $Z_r$ and claim 2.

Reverse: if $\mathcal F|_W\cong\mathcal O_W^r$ then for every $y\in W$ the stalk is free of rank $r$, so $W\subseteq Z_r(\mathcal F)$ and $Z_r$ is a union of such $W$; step 6.1 states exactly this converse and concludes openness. Covering data inside a fixed affine target chart: fix an affine open $U=\operatorname{Spec}R\subseteq S$; then $U$ is quasi-compact, so $X_U=f^{-1}(U)$ is quasi-compact because $f$ is quasi-compact, and the family of all affine open subschemes of $X_U$, which covers $X_U$, has a finite subcover $U_1,\dots,U_n$ (with $n=0$ meaning $X_U=\varnothing$); for each pair $i\le j$ the intersection $U_i\cap U_j$ is quasi-compact by quasi-separatedness, so it has a finite affine cover $U_{ij1},\dots,U_{ijm_{ij}}$, and one may take $U_{ii1}=U_i$. [F2, F9, choose]

Affine model of the comparison: in the situation of step 1.1 regard each $N_{\psi(r)}$ as an $R_r$-module through the canonical ring map $R_r\to C_{\psi(r)}$; then for every $r\in R$ the map $\chi_r:N_r\to N_{\psi(r)}$, $n/r^k\mapsto n/\psi(r)^k$ in fractions, is well defined, $R_r$-linear and bijective: if $n/r^k=n'/r^l$ in $N_r$ then $r^m(r^ln-r^kn')=0$ for some $m$, and applying $\psi$ gives $\psi(r)^m(\psi(r)^ln-\psi(r)^kn')=0$, so the images agree in $N_{\psi(r)}$; every element of $N_{\psi(r)}$ is a fraction $n/\psi(r)^k$, so $\chi_r$ is surjective; and $\chi_r(n/r^k)=0$ means $\psi(r)^mn=0$ for some $m$, hence $r^mn=\psi(r)^mn=0$ and $n/r^k=0$ in $N_r$, so $\chi_r$ is injective; linearity is immediate from the fraction formulas. The affine model is an associated sheaf: in the situation of steps 1.1 and 2.1 the maps $\chi_r$ are compatible with the restriction maps of $\widetilde{N_R}$ and $g_*\mathcal G$, because for $D(s)\subseteq D(r)$ both composites $N_r\to N_{\psi(s)}$ are the canonical localisation maps induced by the ring maps $R_r\to R_s$ and $R_r\to C_{\psi(r)}\to C_{\psi(s)}$; since the distinguished opens form a basis and both sides are sheaves, these compatible isomorphisms on a basis assemble into a unique isomorphism of $\mathcal O_{\operatorname{Spec}R}$-modules $\widetilde{N_R}\to g_*\mathcal G$ whose component on $D(r)$ is $\chi_r$, by restricting a section over an open set to the distinguished opens it contains, mapping each restriction and gluing in the target; the inverses $\chi_r^{-1}$ assemble into an inverse in the same way, so $g_*\mathcal G\cong\widetilde{N_R}$ is quasi-coherent. [F3, F4, F5, F6, step 1.1, step 2.1]

Application to the covering charts: by step 3.1 applied to $g=f|_{U_i}:U_i\to U$ with the quasi-coherent module $\mathcal F|_{U_i}$ one has $(f|_{U_i})_*(\mathcal F|_{U_i})\cong\widetilde{(N_i)_R}$, a quasi-coherent sheaf on $U$; the same argument applies to each chart $f|_{U_{ijk}}:U_{ijk}\to U$ with module $N_{ijk}$, so every summand occurring below is quasi-coherent. Conclusion: by step 5.1 the restriction $(f_*\mathcal F)|_U\cong\ker d$ is the kernel of a morphism of quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_U$-modules, hence is quasi-coherent by [F8]; since the affine open $U\subseteq S$ was arbitrary and affine opens cover $S$, locality of quasi-coherence [F3] shows that $f_*\mathcal F$ itself is quasi-coherent. derivations.claim: An ideal sheaf on an affine chart is associated to its global sections: let $U=\operatorname{Spec}A$ be an affine open and let $\mathcal I\subseteq\mathcal O_X$ be a quasi-coherent ideal sheaf; put $J=\Gamma(U,\mathcal I)$, which is an ideal of $A=\Gamma(U,\mathcal O_X)$ because $\mathcal I$ is an ideal in every section ring. By [F1] applied to the quasi-coherent module $\mathcal I|_U$, the canonical comparison $\widetilde J\to\mathcal I|_U$ is an isomorphism, and naturality of the comparison with respect to the inclusion $\mathcal I\subseteq\mathcal O_X$ shows that it is an isomorphism of subsheaves of $\mathcal O_U=\widetilde A$; hence $\mathcal I|_U=\widetilde J$ and, by [F2], the stalk criterion $\mathcal I_{\mathfrak p}\neq\mathcal O_{U,\mathfrak p}$ holds exactly for $\mathfrak p\in V(J)$, so $V(\mathcal I)\cap U=V(J)$ and $V(\mathcal I)$ is closed in $X$ because the affine charts cover $X$. [F1, F2]

The kernel of a closed immersion is a quasi-coherent ideal sheaf: let $i:Z\to X$ be a closed immersion and put $K=\ker(\mathcal O_X\to i_*\mathcal O_Z)$, computed as a kernel of sheaves, so that $K$ is a subsheaf of $\mathcal O_X$ and an ideal in every section ring. Let $U=\operatorname{Spec}A$ be an affine open of $X$; by the batch-5 supplier [F6] there is an ideal $J\subseteq A$ with $i^{-1}(U)\cong\operatorname{Spec}(A/J)$ and with $i|_U$ the quotient map, so over $U$ the structure map is $\widetilde A\to\widetilde{A/J}$ and [F2] identifies its kernel with $\widetilde J$; hence $K|_U=\widetilde J$ is associated, and because the affine charts cover $X$ the ideal sheaf $K$ satisfies the local definition of quasi-coherence. The uniqueness of $J$ in [F6] shows in addition that the local descriptions agree on overlaps, so $K$ is well defined independently of the charts. This is the exact point where the batch-5 supplier is consumed. [F2, F6]

The affine model of the construction: with $J=\Gamma(U,\mathcal I)$ as in step 1.1, [F2] identifies the quotient $\mathcal O_U/\mathcal I|_U=\mathcal O_U/\widetilde J$ with $\widetilde{A/J}$, and [F3] identifies $\operatorname{Spec}(A/J)$ with the closed subset $V(J)$; the sections of both structure sheaves on the distinguished open $D(\bar f)\subseteq\operatorname{Spec}(A/J)$ corresponding to $D(f)\cap V(J)$ are $(A/J)_f=A_f/J_f$, so the locally ringed space $(V(J),(\mathcal O_U/\widetilde J)|_{V(J)})$ is isomorphic to the affine scheme $\operatorname{Spec}(A/J)$. Consequently every point of $V(\mathcal I)$ has an open neighbourhood in the closed ringed subspace $Z_{\mathcal I}=(V(\mathcal I),(\mathcal O_X/\mathcal I)|_{V(\mathcal I)})$ isomorphic to an affine scheme, and by [F5] the space $Z_{\mathcal I}$ is a scheme. [F2, F3, F5, step 1.1]

The closed immersion is recovered from its kernel: with $K=K_Z$ as in step 1.2, the map $\mathcal O_X\to i_*\mathcal O_Z$ is surjective by the definition of a closed immersion, so it induces an isomorphism of sheaves of rings $\mathcal O_X/K\cong i_*\mathcal O_Z$; moreover $V(K)=\{x:K_x\neq\mathcal O_{X,x}\}=\{x:(i_*\mathcal O_Z)_x\neq0\}$ because $K_x$ is the kernel of the surjection $\mathcal O_{X,x}\to(i_*\mathcal O_Z)_x$, and this set is the image of $i$: for $x=i(z)$ the stalk $(i_*\mathcal O_Z)_x$ is the local ring $\mathcal O_{Z,z}$, which is nonzero for every point of a scheme, while for $x$ outside the closed image the stalk is $0$. Hence the canonical map $Z\to Z_{K}$ (identity on the underlying spaces, the isomorphism $\mathcal O_X/K\cong i_*\mathcal O_Z$ on structure sheaves) is an isomorphism of closed subschemes of $X$ over $X$. [F4, F5, step 1.2]

$Z_{\mathcal I}$ is a closed subscheme with kernel $\mathcal I$: the inclusion $i:Z_{\mathcal I}\to X$ is a homeomorphism onto the closed subset $V(\mathcal I)$ by construction. On each affine chart $U=\operatorname{Spec}A$, step 1.1 gives $\mathcal I|_U=\widetilde J$ and step 2.1 identifies $Z_{\mathcal I}\cap U$ with $\operatorname{Spec}(A/J)$. On every distinguished open $D(f)\subseteq U$, both $(\mathcal O_U/\widetilde J)(D(f))$ and $(i_*\mathcal O_{Z_{\mathcal I}})(D(f))$ are $(A/J)_f$ by [F2], [F4] and step 2.1. Since distinguished opens form a basis, the natural map $\mathcal O_X/\mathcal I\to i_*\mathcal O_{Z_{\mathcal I}}$ is an isomorphism of sheaves. Thus $\mathcal O_X\to i_*\mathcal O_{Z_{\mathcal I}}$ is surjective and $i$ is a closed immersion by [F4], with kernel $\mathcal I$. In the extreme case $\mathcal I=\mathcal O_X$ the quotient is the zero sheaf, whose support is $\varnothing$, giving the empty subscheme; for $\mathcal I=0$ the immersion is the identity of $X$. This constructs $\mathcal I\mapsto Z_{\mathcal I}$ with the asserted properties. [F2, F4, F5, step 1.1, step 2.1]

The two constructions are inverse bijections: starting from a quasi-coherent ideal sheaf $\mathcal I$, step 3.1 gives $K_{Z_{\mathcal I}}=\ker(\mathcal O_X\to\mathcal O_X/\mathcal I)=\mathcal I$, including $\mathcal I=\mathcal O_X$; starting from a closed immersion $i:Z\to X$, step 1.2 gives a quasi-coherent ideal sheaf $K_Z$ and step 2.2 gives $Z_{K_Z}\cong Z$ over $X$. [F6, step 3.1, step 1.2, step 2.2]

a unique ideal $I\subseteq A$ such that, over $U$,
$$i^{-1}(U)\cong\operatorname{Spec}(A/I).$$
Conversely, every quotient map $A\to A/I$ induces a closed immersion
$\operatorname{Spec}(A/I)\to\operatorname{Spec}A$. Every base change of a
closed immersion is a closed immersion. In particular, the empty subscheme of
$\operatorname{Spec}A$ corresponds to $I=A$.

Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $A$ be a commutative
ring with $1$ and put $X=\operatorname{Spec}A$. Let
$\operatorname{Mod}_A$ be the category of $A$-modules and
$\operatorname{QCoh}(X)$ the full subcategory of $\mathcal O_X$-modules
consisting of the quasi-coherent ones ([[def-quasi-coherent-module-scheme]]).

Consider the functors
$$(-)^{\sim}:\operatorname{Mod}_A\longrightarrow\operatorname{QCoh}(X),\qquad M\longmapsto\widetilde M,$$
given by the associated module sheaf
([[def-associated-sheaf-module-affine-scheme]],
[[thm-associated-module-sheaf-exists]]), and
$$\Gamma(X,-):\operatorname{QCoh}(X)\longrightarrow\operatorname{Mod}_A,\qquad \mathcal F\longmapsto\Gamma(X,\mathcal F).$$

Then:

1. For every $A$-module $M$ the canonical map
   $M\to\Gamma(X,\widetilde M)$, $m\mapsto m$ (the section over $X$), is an
   isomorphism of $A$-modules ([[lem-associated-sheaf-sections-basic-open]]).
2. For every quasi-coherent $\mathcal F$ the canonical comparison morphism
   $\kappa_{\mathcal F}:\widetilde{\Gamma(X,\mathcal F)}\to\mathcal F$,
   whose component on $D(f)$ is the localisation at $f$ of the restriction map
   $\Gamma(X,\mathcal F)\to\mathcal F(D(f))$, is an isomorphism of
   $\mathcal O_X$-modules. In particular
   $\mathcal F\cong\widetilde{\Gamma(X,\mathcal F)}$.
3. $(-)^{\sim}$ is fully faithful: for all $A$-modules $M,N$ the map
   $\operatorname{Hom}_A(M,N)\to\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal O_X}(\widetilde M,\widetilde N)$,
   $u\mapsto\widetilde u$, is a bijection, with inverse
   $\psi\mapsto\psi_X$.
4. Consequently $(-)^{\sim}$ and $\Gamma(X,-)$ are quasi-inverse equivalences
   $\operatorname{Mod}_A\simeq\operatorname{QCoh}(X)$: the unit in (1) and the
   counit in (2) are natural isomorphisms, and $M\mapsto\widetilde M$ is an
   equivalence of categories.

All claims include the zero ring $A=0$, where $X=\varnothing$, both categories
are equivalent to the terminal category, and the assertions are trivial. The
Axiom of Choice is used only as it is used by the associated-sheaf existence
theorem and its consequences cited below, and by the compactness of
$\operatorname{Spec}A$.

An ideal sheaf $\mathcal I$ on $X$ is **quasi-coherent** if, for every affine

2. For every family $(M_i)_{i \in I}$ of left $R$-modules, there is a natural isomorphism
$$ S^{-1}\!\left(\bigoplus_{i \in I} M_i\right) \cong \bigoplus_{i \in I} S^{-1}M_i. $$

$$\varphi:(\widetilde M)_{\mathfrak p}\longrightarrow M_{\mathfrak p},\qquad [\text{germ of }s\in\widetilde M(D(f)),\ f\notin\mathfrak p]\longmapsto s/1,$$
where $(\widetilde M)_{\mathfrak p}$ is the stalk of the associated sheaf at
$\mathfrak p$ and $M_{\mathfrak p}$ the localisation of $M$ at the prime
$\mathfrak p$, is an isomorphism of $A_{\mathfrak p}$-modules. It is natural in

$\widetilde u_{\mathfrak p}$ on the left and $u_{\mathfrak p}$ on the right. No
Noetherian or finiteness hypothesis on $M$ is made.

Let $R$ be a commutative ring, let $I\trianglelefteq R$ be an ideal, and let $\pi:R\to R/I$ be the quotient map. Its inverse sends a prime ideal $\mathfrak p\supseteq I$ to $\mathfrak p/I$.

on $Y$ is defined on an open set $V \subseteq Y$ by

Chart dictionary. Let $(V,\mathcal A)$ be a geometric vector bundle with structure morphism $\pi_V$, let $U=\operatorname{Spec}R\subseteq X$ be affine with a graded isomorphism $\mathcal A|_U\cong\operatorname{Sym}(\mathcal O_U^r)$ of the bundle data, and let $D(s)\subseteq U$ be a principal open; then $\pi_V^{-1}(U)\cong\operatorname{Spec}\Gamma(U,\mathcal A) \cong\operatorname{Spec}R[T_1,\dots,T_r]=\mathbf A^r_U$ as $U$-schemes, the chart of $D(s)$ is the restriction with transition the localization $R[T_1,\dots,T_r]\to R[T_1,\dots,T_r]_s$, and the degree-one part is $\mathcal A_1|_U\cong\mathcal O_U^r$. For the total space of a finite locally free $\mathcal E$ the same chart reads $\pi^{-1}(U)\cong\operatorname{Spec}\Gamma(U,\operatorname{Sym}(\mathcal E^\vee))\cong\operatorname{Spec}R[T_1,\dots,T_r]$ whenever $\mathcal E|_U\cong\mathcal O_U^r$. [F1, F3, F4, F5, F6, F8]

The functor $\Phi$. For a geometric vector bundle $(V,\mathcal A)$ the degree-one part $\mathcal A_1$ is finite locally free of rank equal to the rank of the bundle by [F1] and [F2]; put $\Phi(V,\mathcal A):=\mathcal A_1^\vee$, finite locally free of the same rank by [F3]. For a morphism $\varphi:(V,\mathcal A)\to(W,\mathcal B)$ with graded comorphism $\varphi^\sharp:\mathcal B\to\mathcal A$, put $\Phi(\varphi):=(\varphi^\sharp_1)^\vee:\mathcal A_1^\vee\to\mathcal B_1^\vee$, an $\mathcal O_X$-linear map of finite locally free modules [F3]. Identities and composites are preserved: $\Phi(\mathrm{id})=\mathrm{id}$, and for a second morphism $\omega:(W,\mathcal B)\to(Z,\mathcal C)$ one has $(\omega\circ\varphi)^\sharp_1=\varphi^\sharp_1\circ\omega^\sharp_1$, whose transpose is $(\omega^\sharp_1)^\vee\circ(\varphi^\sharp_1)^\vee= \Phi(\omega)\circ\Phi(\varphi)$. Hence $\Phi$ is a covariant functor $\operatorname{GVB}(X)\to\operatorname{FLF}(X)$ preserving ranks. [F1, F2, F3, F13]

Induced morphism from a graded algebra map. Let $\mathcal A,\mathcal B$ be graded $\mathcal O_X$-algebras that are locally polynomial in the sense that their relative coordinate algebras admit the charts of step 1.2 for the same covering opens; then every graded $\mathcal O_X$-algebra map $\psi:\mathcal B\to\mathcal A$ induces an $X$-morphism $\Psi(\psi):\operatorname{Spec}_X\mathcal A\to \operatorname{Spec}_X\mathcal B$ with comorphism $\psi$. Construction: cover $X$ by the affine opens $U=\operatorname{Spec}R$ over which both algebras are graded free of ranks $s$ and $r$; the global sections map $\psi(U):R[T_1,\dots,T_s]\to R[T_1,\dots,T_r]$ is an $R$-algebra map by [F10] under the chart identifications of [F6], giving the $U$-morphism $\operatorname{Spec}(\psi(U))$ between the charts by [F9]. These chart morphisms glue: for a principal open $D(t)\subseteq U$ the restriction of $\psi(U)$ is $\psi(D(t))$ by [F10], so $\operatorname{Spec}(\psi(D(t)))$ is the restriction of $\operatorname{Spec}(\psi(U))$ to the subchart by [F8] and [F9]; hence all chart morphisms agree on overlaps after refining by affine opens, and they glue to an $X$-morphism $\Psi(\psi)$ because the source is covered by the charts and its structure sheaf is a sheaf [F11]. The comorphism of $\Psi(\psi)$ restricts to $\psi(U)$ on each chart, whence it equals $\psi$ [F10, F11]. [F4, F5, F6, F8, F9, F10, F11, F12]

If $\varphi,\varphi':\operatorname{Spec}_X\mathcal A\to \operatorname{Spec}_X\mathcal B$ are $X$-morphisms with the same comorphism $\psi:\mathcal B\to\mathcal A$, then on each chart $U$ of step 2.1 the restrictions are morphisms of the affine schemes $\operatorname{Spec}\Gamma(U,\mathcal A)\to \operatorname{Spec}\Gamma(U,\mathcal B)$ with the same global section map $\psi(U)$, hence equal by [F9]; the charts cover the source, so $\varphi=\varphi'$ by [F11]. Therefore the comorphism assignment $\Theta:\varphi\mapsto\varphi^\sharp$ is a bijection from the set of grading-preserving $X$-morphisms $\operatorname{Spec}_X\mathcal A\to\operatorname{Spec}_X\mathcal B$ onto the graded $\mathcal O_X$-algebra maps $\mathcal B\to\mathcal A$, with two-sided inverse $\Psi$ by step 2.1. Finally $\Psi(\psi\circ\psi')=\Psi(\psi')\circ\Psi(\psi)$ for graded maps $\psi:\mathcal B\to\mathcal A$ and $\psi':\mathcal C\to\mathcal B$: both sides are $X$-morphisms $\operatorname{Spec}_X\mathcal A\to \operatorname{Spec}_X\mathcal C$ with comorphism $\psi\circ\psi'$, and such a morphism is unique; likewise $\Psi(\mathrm{id})=\mathrm{id}$. Full faithfulness. For finite locally free $\mathcal E,\mathcal F$ the comorphism bijection of step 3.1, applied to $\mathcal A=\operatorname{Sym}(\mathcal E^\vee)$ and $\mathcal B=\operatorname{Sym}(\mathcal F^\vee)$, identifies morphisms $\mathbb V(\mathcal E)\to\mathbb V(\mathcal F)$ of geometric vector bundles with graded algebra maps $\operatorname{Sym}(\mathcal F^\vee)\to \operatorname{Sym}(\mathcal E^\vee)$, which by the universal property of [F4] correspond bijectively to $\mathcal O_X$-linear maps $\mathcal F^\vee\to\mathcal E^\vee=(\operatorname{Sym}(\mathcal E^\vee))_1$, that is, by the double dual isomorphism of [F3], to $\mathcal O_X$-linear maps $\mathcal E\to\mathcal F$; the resulting bijection sends $\alpha$ to $\mathbb V(\alpha)$ by step 4.1, with inverse $\varphi\mapsto\varepsilon_{\mathcal F}\circ(\varphi^\sharp_1)^\vee\circ \operatorname{ev}_{\mathcal E}$. Indeed for $\alpha$ the composite is $\alpha$ by the naturality identity of step 5.1, and for $\varphi$ the induced map $\alpha$ satisfies $\alpha^\vee=\varphi^\sharp_1$ because double transposition returns the original map, so $\operatorname{Sym}(\alpha^\vee)=\varphi^\sharp$ since a graded algebra map out of $\operatorname{Sym}(\mathcal F^\vee)$ is determined by its degree-one part, and hence $\mathbb V(\alpha)=\varphi$ by step 3.1. [F3, F4, step 3.1, step 4.1, step 5.1]

Choice accounting. The Axiom of Choice is used only through the associated-sheaf, gluing, symmetric-algebra and relative-spectrum constructions inherited in [F1] and [F4] to [F7], as recorded in [F14]; the constructions of this proof range over the families of all affine charts on which the algebras are graded free and of all module morphisms, and select no simultaneous family of charts, generators or isomorphisms. The rank of each side is determined independently of charts by [F2], so the equivalence and the rank correspondence are stated in the inherited AC theory. [F2, F14] ∎

boundaries.evidence: For $X=\varnothing$ the only $\mathcal O_X$-module is $0$, which satisfies the Definition of finite local freeness vacuously, and step 1.2 gives $\mathbb V(0)=\operatorname{Spec}_\varnothing\mathcal O_\varnothing=\varnothing$; both categories are then equivalent to the terminal category, the unit of step 4.2 and the counit of step 5.1 being identity isomorphisms. No chart is selected, so the empty cover causes no gap.

For the zero module the Definition gives $\mathbb V(0)=X$ (rank-$0$ bundle) and step 1.3 gives $\Phi(\mathbb V(0))=0^{\vee}=0$; the counit $\varepsilon_0:(0^\vee)^\vee\to0$ of step 5.1 is the identity isomorphism, so the zero object is fixed up to canonical isomorphism.

The rank-one case is the single-chart case $\mathcal E=\mathcal O_X$: step 1.2 gives $\mathbb V(\mathcal O_X)=\operatorname{Spec}_X\mathcal O_X[T_1]\cong\mathbf A^1_X$ with the degree-one generator, and step 6.2 shows the morphism bijection $\operatorname{Hom}(\mathcal E,\mathcal F)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{\rm GVB}(\mathbb V(\mathcal E),\mathbb V(\mathcal F))$ for all ranks, in particular rank one.

The degenerate shape admitted by the Definition is a locally constant but non-constant rank, e.g. $X=Y\sqcup Z$ with $\mathcal E$ of rank $0$ on $Y$ and rank $1$ on $Z$: $\mathbb V(\mathcal E)|_Y=Y$ and $\mathbb V(\mathcal E)|_Z\cong\mathbf A^1_Z$ by step 1.2, and the unit of step 4.2 is computed chartwise, so both the unit and the counit are defined without any global constancy assumption.

The endpoint values of the rank parameter are $0$, treated in step 5.1 by $\varepsilon_0$ and $\mathbb V(0)=X$, and the endpoint of the chart index is the single open $U=X$ when $X$ is affine with $\mathcal E$ free; the extreme open $W=\varnothing$ appears in the restriction isomorphism of [F5], which is the identity on the empty piece.

Step 7.1 records that the proof ranges over the families of all affine charts on which the algebras are graded free and of all module morphisms, that no simultaneous family of charts, generators or isomorphisms is selected, and that the Axiom of Choice is used only as inherited in [F1] and [F4] to [F7]; the ranks are chart-independent by [F2].

Forward direction: for a finite locally free $\mathcal E$ the Definition makes $\operatorname{Sym}(\mathcal E^\vee)$ affine-locally module-associated and step 4.1 defines the covariant functor $\mathbb V$ on morphisms via $\alpha\mapsto\operatorname{Sym}(\alpha^\vee)$, with rank preservation checked in steps 1.2 and 4.1.

Reverse direction: every geometric vector bundle $(V,\mathcal A)$ in the sense of the Definition has $\mathcal A_1$ finite locally free (step 1.3) and is canonically isomorphic to $\mathbb V(\Phi(V,\mathcal A))=\operatorname{Spec}_X\operatorname{Sym}(\mathcal A_1)$ by the multiplication isomorphism of step 4.2, so $\mathbb V$ is essentially surjective with quasi-inverse $\Phi$ (step 6.1).
